As most Level 3 ("fast") charging stations only have a single plug type, EV owners have to find a charger which matches the ports in their car. 12 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications 3 Legacy Device Lifecycle Legacy device replacement decisions involve multiple interconnected factors beyond simple technical obsolescence. Analysis of replacement patterns across grid, transportation, and building systems reveals four primary drivers: supply chain constraints that limit continued operation, physical and performance degradation over operational lifespans, availability of enhanced features in newer technologies, and funding cycles that govern capital investment timing. Replacement trigger timing varies substantially across sectors and equipment types. Grid infrastructure may operate for decades before encountering supply chain limitations, while transportation and building infrastructure experience more rapid degradation due to environmental exposure. Understanding these lifecycle patterns enables more effective infrastructure modernization planning and strategic resource allocation across these critical systems. 3.1 Supply Chain Issues The lifecycle management of legacy devices presents unique supply chain challenges that differ significantly from modern equipment procurement and maintenance. Legacy devices often rely on obsolete components, discontinued manufacturing processes, and specialized materials that are no longer in regular production. Replacement parts can take much longer to procure than modern devices, or they may have to be custom-ordered and produced. 3.2 Equipment Degradation There are different causes of equipment degradation in device lifecycles. Large equipment typically has an expected lifecycle end, e.g. 20 years for HVAC systems. However the equipment lifespan can be affected by a variety of factors. • Weather: Equipment that is exposed to the elements may degrade faster than it might in a different environ- ment. This issue can affect everything from above-the-ground sensors, loop detectors (breakage in the road damages loops), or a build-up of dirt. Distribution transformers are sensitive to heat. • Insufficient Maintenance: Most equipment requires regular maintenance but for some equipment this is es- pecially urgent.
